name: status-code
purpose: Use StatusCode only for an HTTP status code or method (200, 404, GET); for resource state use StatusIndicator, and for any other word use Tag. StatusCode shows the HTTP status of a request, optionally preceded by its method, as one compact monospace pill whose colour comes from the status class: informational, success and redirect responses (1xx, 2xx, 3xx) stay neutral, client errors (4xx) take the warning colour and server errors (5xx) the danger colour, so failures stand out in a long request log without every successful row competing for attention. Anything that is not a status from 100 to 599 renders muted, as written. It composes `Tag` for the surface, so its sizes, shape and colours are the tag's; the component owns only the mapping from status to colour and the method plus code layout that every logs table would otherwise repeat.
useWhen: A request log, an invocation list or a trace detail shows the HTTP status of each request (`GET 200`, `POST 503`).
A detail panel summarizes the response of one request next to its timing and size.
avoidWhen: The status is a resource lifecycle (`Active`, `Pending`, `Failed`) → use `tag` or `Table.CellStatus`.
The value is a security or incident level → use `severity-tag`.
A dot that says whether a service is up → use `status-indicator`.
related: tag` — the surface StatusCode composes; use it directly for statuses that are not HTTP codes.
table` — place StatusCode inside a `#cell-<id>` slot of a request log.
severity-tag` — ordered severity levels with a bar glyph.
bestPractices: Pass the status as it comes from the log (`404` or `'404'`); the component derives the colour, so do not pick a colour per row.
Pass `method` only when the list mixes methods; a list of `GET` requests reads better with the code alone.
Keep the column narrow: the pill never wraps and is at most `GET` plus three digits wide for real traffic.

props.name: code
props.doc: HTTP status, as a number or a string (`404`, `'404'`). 1xx to 3xx render neutral, 4xx warning, 5xx danger; anything else renders muted as written, empty a dash.

props.name: method
props.doc: Request method shown before the code (`GET`, `POST`), upper-cased. Empty shows the code alone.

props.name: size
props.doc: Size token forwarded to `Tag`; `medium` is 24px tall, `small` is 20px.

examples.name: Default
Sizes
Request log
examples.sfc:
<script setup>
  import DataTable from '@aziontech/webkit/data-table'
  import StatusCode from '@aziontech/webkit/status-code'

  const rows = [
    { id: 'r1', time: '12:04:31', method: 'GET', status: 200, path: '/', duration: '38 ms' },
    {
      id: 'r2',
      time: '12:04:29',
      method: 'GET',
      status: 304,
      path: '/assets/app.js',
      duration: '4 ms'
    },
    {
      id: 'r3',
      time: '12:04:27',
      method: 'POST',
      status: 503,
      path: '/api/orders',
      duration: '1.2 s'
    },
    {
      id: 'r4',
      time: '12:04:22',
      method: 'GET',
      status: 200,
      path: '/api/products',
      duration: '61 ms'
    },
    {
      id: 'r5',
      time: '12:04:19',
      method: 'DELETE',
      status: 404,
      path: '/api/carts/42',
      duration: '12 ms'
    },
    { id: 'r6', time: '12:04:15', method: 'GET', status: 200, path: '/docs', duration: '45 ms' }
  ]

  const columns = [
    { accessorKey: 'time', header: 'Time', minWidth: 96 },
    { accessorKey: 'status', header: 'Status', minWidth: 120 },
    { accessorKey: 'path', header: 'Path', grow: 3, principal: true },
    { accessorKey: 'duration', header: 'Duration', minWidth: 96, align: 'end' }
  ]
</script>

<template>
  <DataTable
    :data="rows"
    :columns="columns"
    density="compact"
    aria-label="Requests to app.example.com"
  >
    <template #cell-status="{ row }">
      <StatusCode
        :code="row.status"
        :method="row.method"
      />
    </template>
  </DataTable>
</template>
